articles.title: B/R's Week 6 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: We're heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and fantasy managers face a range of outlooks based on their records.
articles.body:
We're heading into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, and fantasy managers face a range of outlooks based on their records.

For those at 4-1, everything is coming up roses. At 3-2, there's room for improvement, but they're still on the right side of .500.

Conversely, a 2-3 start isn't ideal, but it's more manageable than 1-4, especially for managers dealing with injuries and disappointing production.

Regardless of their circumstances, all fantasy managers have one thing in common: They want a win in Week 6. We want to help you do just that with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to this week's player rankings (which include the top 124 players overall to assist in making "flex" lineup calls), a few quick notes.

The first is the same as always—the overall rankings do not include quarterbacks. If your league employs a "superflex" spot and you have a viable QB2, start them there. Even mediocre signal-callers are generally more consistent as flex options.

The second is that Week 6 is the first four-team bye week—the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings are all off. This may be the only week that Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs doesn't blow up.

Finally, if you're sitting at 1-4 and in last place, the last thing you want from this writer is a pep talk. Believe me, I know your pain. But don't look at the hole you're in as one big problem. Break it down into smaller ones. Treat every week like a mini-season all its own. Make some waiver-wire moves, and don't be afraid to be bold with your lineup decisions.

Find a way to eke out a win in Week 6 and then try to stack a few victories.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is one of one.

For most quarterbacks, completing just 12 passes and throwing just a single touchdown pass would portend at best a mediocre fantasy week. But Allen is not most quarterbacks—despite just 210 passing yards against the Los Angeles Rams, Allen also ran for 121 yards and another touchdown on the way to finishing third in fantasy points among quarterbacks for the week.

Allen now has eight rushing scores for the season and is the highest-scoring quarterback by a wide margin.

Paying up for him this year may not have been such a bad idea after all.

Josh Allen wasn't the only quarterback who piled up rushing yards in Week 5—in his return from a dislocated elbow, Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders ran for 103 yards and a pair of scores against the New York Giants.

Drake Maye of the New England Patriots started the season slowly—Maye failed to amass 10 fantasy points in any of his first three starts. But Maye has been on fire the past two weeks—including 374 passing yards, four touchdown passes and a rushing score last week against the Las Vegas Raiders.

There's some optimism that Lamar Jackson (ankle) of the Baltimore Ravens will be able to return in Week 6—so much so that he's included in this week's rankings. But Tyler Huntley played well in Jackson's stead—if the Ravens play it safe and sit Jackson another week Huntley would check in as a decent QB2 against the Cleveland Browns.

Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (vs. Washington Commanders)

Purdy has gone from a low-end fantasy QB1 in drafts over the summer to the highest-scoring fantasy quarterback in the NFC. The good times will keep rolling on Monday night against Washington's 29th-ranked pass defense.

Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys (at Green Bay Packers)

Many fantasy managers will have little recourse but to roll Prescott out Sunday night against the Packers. But Prescott has quietly had just one 20-point game this season and draws a bottom-five fantasy matchup for the position at Lambeau Field.

Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Cousins has quietly been a top-10 fantasy quarterback over the first five weeks of the season, and he could have another solid outing in Week 6. The Bills are doing many things well right now, but playing defense is not one of them.

The Pittsburgh Steelers opened the season with a committee backfield, but while Rico Dowdle (toe) has been sidelined, Jaylen Warren has done his level best to establish himself as the team's lead back.

Warren has been nothing short of outstanding the past few weeks. After piling up 181 total yards and two touchdowns last week against the Indianapolis Colts, he has averaged 107 rushing yards a game over that span, adding just over 40 yards per contest over that same stretch.

Warren is fourth in PPR points among running backs over the last three weeks, and head coach Mike McCarthy has called him " the man " in the Pittsburgh backfield.

Injuries continued to mount in the backfield in Week 5. David Montgomery of the Houston Texans (groin) and TreVeyon Henderson of the New England Patriots (ankle) both left their games early. Quinshon Judkins of the Cleveland Browns (ankle) finished the loss to the New York Jets, but he was spotted in a walking boot after the game.

The Philadelphia Eagles may have to hold running back tryouts in the parking lot of The Linc—with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and backup Will Shipley (foot) both expected to miss Week 6, Dameon Pierce has rapidly gone from the practice squad to Philly's lead back.

Entering the season, Omarion Hampton of the Los Angeles Chargers was viewed as a rising talent and fringe RB1. But the Bolts have struggled, and Hampton is sharing work in a three-headed backfield. He ranks as RB36 in PPR scoring through five weeks.

Emanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks (at Denver Broncos)

Wilson has scored on the ground each of the last two weeks, although he also fumbled in both of those games. The fourth-year veteran will make it three games in a row with a touchdown this week against a surprisingly porous Denver defense.

Woody Marks, Houston Texans (at Jacksonville Jaguars, London)

With David Montgomery on the shelf, Marks will be a popular player on waiver wires this week. But he should be benched where possible in Week 6—the Jaguars led the league in run defense last year and are right back in that spot in 2026.

Dameon Pierce, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Pierce was not great last week in London, gaining just 14 yards on 11 carries. The sledding should be significantly easier this week against the Panthers, who have surrendered 156.5 yards per game on the ground in 2026.

The Los Angeles Rams came up just short Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. But wide receiver Puka Nacua can't be blamed for the setback that dropped the Rams to 2-3 for the season.

Nacua has missed time this season, but when he's been out there, he has been productive, culminating in a ridiculous 17/138/1 stat line against the Bills.

Nacua is averaging just over eight yards per catch this season—not very Nacua-like—but he was Week 5's highest-scoring wideout. He's averaging a jaw-dropping 15 targets per game, and only Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba is averaging more PPR points per game.

Nacua now looks poised for another big week against the Arizona Cardinals.

The list of banged-up wide receivers continues to grow. Although fantasy managers got Justin Jefferson back in Week 5, several other receivers suffered injuries.

Deebo Samuel Sr. of the San Francisco 49ers hurt his hamstring, CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys sustained a quad contusion, and Roman Wilson of the Pittsburgh Steelers is expected to miss time with a finger injury.

Among this year's high-scorers at wide receiver in fantasy leagues, the biggest early surprise may well be Christian Watson of the Green Bay Packers. Watson caught two long touchdown passes in last week's win over the rival Bears, and he's third at the position in PPR points after five weeks.

The trade last weekend that sent Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston has rekindled hopes that the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft can resurrect his lagging career. But now Harrison has to learn a new offense, and Nico Collins is the unquestioned alpha in that passing game. Harrison's still an end-of-the-bench fantasy reserve.

Luther Burden III, Chicago Bears (at Atlanta Falcons)

Burden's production has taken a hit with all the shakeups at quarterback in the Windy City. But if Caleb Williams can't play Sunday, Case Keenum should get the nod—and he frequently targeted Burden in his first start this year.

Ladd McConkey, Los Angeles Chargers (at Kansas City Chiefs)

McConkey's disastrous 2026 season continued in Week 5—he was active but didn't play a snap against the Broncos. Now he gets a Chiefs team allowing the fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts five weeks into the season.

Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Tucker has been relatively quiet since a big outing in Week 2, but if ever there was a week for him to have another huge game, this is it. The Buffalo pass defense is a sieve, and the Raiders are going to have to throw to keep up with the Bills offense.

That Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders sits fifth in fantasy points among tight ends might seem a little disappointing at first glance—until you realize he has only played three games.

Since missing the first two games of the season with a knee injury, Bowers has been highly productive. Even in last week's blowout loss to the New England Patriots, he caught eight of 10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown.

Bowers has topped 20 PPR points in all three of his starts this year, and his 23.7 PPR points per game is more than 5.5 points higher than Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals.

Tight ends haven't been hit by injuries as hard as wide receivers, but a couple of players at the position went down. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq of the New York Jets and T.J. Hockenson of the Minnesota Vikings both suffered concussions.

Minnesota's Week 6 bye gives Hockenson additional time to recover before the team's next game.

Isaiah Likely of the New York Giants was a trendy breakout pick in 2026, and through five weeks at least he deserves some credit. He was the highest-scoring tight end of Week 5 thanks to an 11/94/2 line, and he sits second at the position in PPR points for the season.

It may be time to start having uncomfortable conversations about Colston Loveland of the Chicago Bears. Last week in Titletown, Loveland had two catches for 19 yards, and he barely has more PPR points for the season than Bowers is averaging per game.

Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

After five catches for 83 yards last week against the Buffalo Bills, Higbee sits sixth in PPR points at tight end over the last three weeks. Meanwhile, the Cardinals have given up the fifth-most PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

Kyle Pitts, Atlanta Falcons (vs. Chicago Bears)

Pitts caught five passes for 42 yards and a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5. However, he faces a tougher fantasy matchup Sunday against a Bears team allowing the third-fewest PPR points to tight ends this season.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

With eight catches for 61 yards and three touchdowns over the last two weeks, it might be a stretch to call Freiermuth a "sleeper." His productive stretch could continue this week in a plus fantasy matchup for tight ends with the Buccaneers.

Kickers are changing late-game strategy across the NFL.

In just the past few weeks, we have seen a pair of games decided by kickers hitting a 57-yarder as time expired. Both teams had less than 10 seconds left when the ball was kicked off to them.

But a touchback followed by a 25-yard completion—or a long kickoff return—can put a team at the opponent's 40-yard line. A kicker like Jacksonville's Cam Little can bang it through from there with room to spare—with a defensive tackle snapping the ball, no less.

What used to be desperation kicks that only a couple of kickers in the league had a real chance to hit are now commonplace.

We are going to see a 70-yard field goal soon.

For the most part, the Houston Texans defense has disappointed to this point in the season. But edge-rusher Will Anderson Jr. can't be blamed for those struggles—after three sacks last week against the Tennessee Titans, Anderson has an NFL-high 7.5 sacks for the year.

It wasn't supposed to be this way, but the Los Angeles Chargers have become an offense to target with fantasy defenses, allowing the most fantasy points per game to the position in the AFC. With the Kansas City Chiefs coming off their bye and playing at home, they are an elite fantasy play in Week 6.

Five weeks in, five kickers have attempted at least 10 field goals without a miss: Spencer Shrader, Will Reichard, Evan McPherson, Jason Myers and Andre Szmyt.

New England Patriots Defense (vs. New York Jets)

After a rocky start to the season, the Patriots have rebounded in a big way the past two weeks, with the defense playing a big part. Over the last 15-plus years, the Jets have one win at Gillette Stadium. One.

Spencer Shrader, Indianapolis Colts (vs. Tennessee Titans)

Since Week 2, Shrader has peeled off four straight games with at least 12 fantasy points. Now, fantasy's highest-scoring kicker gets a Titans team allowing the most fantasy points per game to kickers this year.

Las Vegas Raiders Defense (vs. Buffalo Bills)

The run with the Raiders defense was fun while it lasted—but it's over. The Raiders have fallen out of the top-12 after back-to-back clunkers in bad matchups, and now Vegas hosts the buzzsaw that is the Buffalo Bills offense.

Tyler Bass, Buffalo Bills (at Las Vegas Raiders)

After his game-winning heroics on Monday night, Bass has climbed into the top 10 among fantasy kickers for the season. But the Raiders have been giving up far more extra points than field-goal attempts the past couple of weeks.

Baltimore Ravens Defense (at Cleveland Browns)

The Ravens haven't been especially relevant in fantasy—the team barely ranks inside the top 20 in fantasy points. But this week Baltimore draws a reeling Browns offense that just allowed eight sacks to the New York Jets.

Chris Boswell, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Boswell is one of this writer's favorite kickers—a steady veteran on a good (but not great) offense. Throw in a top-five fantasy matchup for his position with the Buccaneers this week, and you have the recipe for success.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: “He could be facing a significant suspension”: Tyreek Hill’s future hangs in the balance as civil trial testimony raises questions about a potential Chiefs reunion
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ star player, has found himself in controversial legal trouble as his estranged wife, popular entrepreneur and
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ star player, has found himself in controversial legal trouble as his estranged wife, popular entrepreneur and social media influencer Keeta Vaccaro has now accused him of domestic violence. This has also affected his career in the league as coupled with his brutal injuries, Tyreek Hill’s future remains in limbo even as there are rumors about Kansas City Chiefs being interested in him.Tyreek Hill’s future in the league turns more uncertain even amid the rumors about Kansas City Chiefs signing himA few hours ago Pro Football Talk's NFL insider Mike Florio noted in a recent report, "The NFL's pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation of Hill based on abuse allegations made by his ex-wife, Keeta Vaccaro, has taken a back seat to a civil trial that started on Tuesday. In it, Vaccaro seeks compensation for multiple instances of assault and battery."Pro Football Talk's NFL insider Mike Florio added, "If, in the end, the NFL's investigators believe Vaccaro more than they believe Hill, he could be facing a significant suspension. In theory, each incident of alleged abuse could spark a six-game baseline suspension. The trial testimony to date makes the out-of-the-blue effort to get Hill on an NFL team even more strange.”Pro Football Talk's NFL insider Mike Florio continued, “Whatever the strategy for introducing the notion of Hill signing with the Chiefs or some other team on the eve of the civil trial, the civil trial significantly complicates his desire to play again.”He added, “Even if the NFL doesn't choose to banish him with the opportunity to apply for reinstatement after a year — the strongest punishment available under the Personal Conduct Policy — what team in its right mind would sign him after the testimony of the past few days?"However, the 8 time Pro Bowler Tyreek Hill has kept himself away from all the negative speculations about his future in the league.Why did Tyreek Hill’s year long marriage to Keeta Vaccaro end abruptly?At this point in time, all that the popular wide receiver Tyreek Hill is focusing on is testifying in court as he continues to fight with his estranged wife, keeta Vaccaro.For the unversed, Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro tied the knot in 2023 but by last year, their high profile marriage had already ended as she accused him of domestic violence and filed for a divorce, hours after authorities were called to their place in Miami.Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro had also welcomed a daughter in December 2024, Capri, and for now, she remains with her mother as the popular wide receiver recovers from the brutal injuries he sustained in the last season while playing for the Miami Dolphins.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady missed four games over Deflategate 10 years ago, but the NFL’s controversial punishment still sparks debate
articles.summary: Tom Brady returned to the New England Patriots on October 9, 2016, after serving a four-game suspension over Deflategate, helping his team beat the
articles.body: Tom Brady returned to the New England Patriots on October 9, 2016, after serving a four-game suspension over Deflategate, helping his team beat the Cleveland Browns 33-13. A decade later, the punishment remains a source of disagreement among NFL fans, former players and sports commentators. The league accused Brady of being aware of the use of under-inflated footballs during the 2015 AFC Championship Game, an allegation he denied throughout the dispute. The case triggered a lengthy legal fight and cost the NFL millions of dollars, leaving a question that has never quite gone away: did Brady deserve to miss those four games?Tom Brady’s Deflategate suspension followed a lengthy legal battleThe controversy began after the Patriots beat the Indianapolis Colts in the AFC Championship Game in January 2015. An NFL investigation led by general counsel Jeff Pash and attorney Ted Wells examined whether New England personnel had deliberately deflated footballs.According to ESPN’s report on the investigation, the league concluded it was “‘more probable than not’ that Patriots personnel deliberately deflated footballs during the AFC Championship Game, and that Brady was probably ‘at least generally aware’ of the rules violation.”Brady received a four-game suspension without pay. A federal judge overturned the punishment in September 2015, offering him a temporary victory. The NFL successfully reinstated it in April 2016, however, and the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected Brady’s appeal that May.The quarterback consequently missed New England’s first four regular-season games in 2016. He returned against Cleveland in Week 5, throwing for 406 yards and three touchdowns in the Patriots’ comfortable win.The dispute had already stretched far beyond the football field. ESPN reported that the NFL spent roughly $22 million over two years investigating the allegations, pursuing legal action and disciplining the organization.Darrelle Revis and Brady’s father revealed the personal tollFor Brady, Deflategate was not simply a fight over equipment rules or a suspension. Darrelle Revis, his former teammate in New England, recalled seeing the quarterback struggle emotionally when he addressed the team.“When the Deflategate happened, and Tom was the headliner of the whole situation, he addressed us as a team. You can tell he was distraught,” Revis said on Apple TV+’s documentary The Dynasty.Revis said Brady directly rejected the allegations in front of his teammates.“He said, ‘This is something I wouldn’t do. I would not ruin the season for us. The allegations are false.’ He was actually bawling his eyes out in front of us.”Brady’s father, Tom Brady Sr., also described the strain the controversy placed on the family.“It was extraordinarily difficult in the life of the Brady family,” he said in the documentary. “Not only did I suffer from it, but my wife, it crushed her. Because he’s not a liar.”Those accounts offer a different perspective on a case often reduced to arguments about football pressure and competitive advantage. Brady’s supporters saw a player fighting a punishment he believed was unjust, with his reputation and family life caught in the fallout.Jason Kelce and Bob Costas questioned the NFL’s responseBrady himself later found humor in the league’s costly investigation. During his Netflix roast in May 2024, he took a swipe at the money spent pursuing the case.“If they had given me the $20 million, I would have just told them I f---ing did it,” Brady quipped.Former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce was more direct about his opposition to the punishment. Speaking on the New Heights podcast, he said, “I don’t even think Tom should have gotten in trouble for deflating footballs. I’m pro deflating footballs. I’ll say it. I’ll say it. I am pro deflating footballs.”Kelce continued, “He outsmarted people. Why the f--- does it matter how much air is in that motherf-----?”The former center added, “If you’re throwing it and catching it, who the f--- cares?”Veteran sportscaster Bob Costas also criticized the league’s handling of the scandal in 2015. He argued that officials had “overreacted” and “turned a misdemeanor into a federal case, both figuratively and literally.”Costas compared the situation to other forms of competitive gamesmanship, including watering down a playing field to slow an opponent or using pine tar on a bat. He acknowledged that Brady’s own response had contributed to the controversy, saying the league “perhaps overreacted and Brady himself didn’t say what he could’ve said.”Ten years on, Deflategate remains a revealing test of how the NFL handles discipline, evidence and public trust. Brady served the suspension, returned to win games and later won another Super Bowl with New England. Yet the punishment still divides opinion, partly because the league's findings, the legal fight and the personal accounts have never produced a universally accepted verdict among fans.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Top WR Targets After Marvin Harrison Jr. Dealt to Texans
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. may not be the last notable wide receiver to move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. may not be the last notable wide receiver to move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler cited multiple wideouts who could plausibly be dealt over the next few weeks.

The Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. is the first name Graziano mentioned because the 2024 first-round pick is going backwards for the second straight season. He has just nine receptions for 105 yards and one touchdown.

Fowler questioned whether the Jaguars would trade Thomas given their 4-1 start, and the NFL insider cited how Thomas' value goes a little beyond the raw stats.

"His immense skill set requires defensive backs to play him deep, which opens the field for Washington and Meyers," Fowler said. "But if Jacksonville gets a good offer, it would be foolish not to consider it."

He had a similar opinion on the Cleveland Browns' Jerry Jeudy, who has fallen behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the pecking order.

"The Browns are improved and need veteran help, so my sense is while they are not actively shopping Jeudy, a strong offer could change that," Fowler reported.

He went on to say that Los Angeles Chargers receiver Quentin Johnston "has come up in a few of my recent conversations."

The Chargers are 0-5, so they could wave the white flag and be a seller at the deadline before too long. Graziano spoke to one source who's skeptical L.A. has that much that other teams will want, though.

In the case of Johnston, his production (seven receptions and 108 yards) isn't very good, and he has a $16.5 million option for 2027. His market could be limited.

Fowler closed out the conversation by throwing the Baltimore Ravens' Rashod Bateman and Minnesota Vikings' Jauan Jennings into the mix.

In general, there are opportunities out there for teams in need of receiver help. However, all of the candidates on the board either carry some risk or are likely to have limited upside.

articles.title: Simone Biles reveals how her embarrassing skin condition journey inspired Arcutis Biotherapeutics awareness campaign
articles.summary: Talk about a warrior - on the spring floor as well as outside of it.
articles.body: Talk about a warrior - on the spring floor as well as outside of it. Olympic gymnast Simone Biles recently opened up about a personal health struggle that left her feeling self-conscious.But she thoughtfully turned her embarrassing experience with an inflammatory skin condition into an awareness campaign for Arcutis Biotherapeutics.Indianapolis Colts safety Jonathan Owens’ wife has partnered with the biopharmaceutical company for its “Skin to Believe In” campaign. The initiative encourages people living with eczema and seborrheic dermatitis to seek medical help and explore treatment options.The campaign was announced on September 29; it draws attention to skin conditions that cause persistent itching, flaking, and visible changes.According to Arcutis Biotherapeutics, nearly 36 million Americans suffer from inflammatory skin conditions like seborrheic dermatitis and the most common form of eczema - atopic dermatitis.Simone Biles, wife of Jonathan Owens, reveals eczema struggleIn a Healthline interview, Simone Biles revealed that she mistook itching and flaking on her scalp for dandruff. She even worried that the symptoms could be contagious. Beyond her scalp troubles, she also noticed recurring dry patches on her arms.These skin symptoms became frustrating, particularly during her gymnastic training. She would catch herself scratching on the uneven bars or balance beam while waiting her turn to come. She would scratch until she bled.She felt uncomfortable about how the flakes showed up on camera during photoshoots. She would try to conceal them with oils.The Olympic gold medalist had spent years experimenting with over-the-counter products. She tried several shampoos, creams, and oils. But nothing relieved her skin condition. Embarrassment and demanding training schedules delayed her from seeking professional help for her skin ailment.Biles finally revealed her skin sorrows on social media during the 2024 Paris Olympics. Immediately thereafter, she sought skin help from a dermatologist. She finally found a name for her condition. She was diagnosed with seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, while she had eczema [atopic dermatitis] on her arms.Zoryve treatment helps manage skin symptomsAfter she found a name for her unknown skin condition, Simone Biles finally embraced relief with Zoryve [roflumilast]. Arcutis Biotherapeutics developed this prescription topical medication - the 0.3% foam formulation relieved her seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, while the 0.15% cream helped her eczema on her arms.She praised the treatment, saying it easily fit into her busy routine. She found the medication non-greasy, easy-to-use, and stressed that it’s not a steroid, pill, injection, or shampoo. The timely treatment reduced Biles’ itching and flaking problem. The eczema patches on her arms also became clear.Caution note: individual effects can vary, so patients should consult a healthcare professional before starting treatment to determine appropriate options.Arcutis campaign aims to break skin condition stigmaSimone Biles collaborated with Arcutis Biotherapeutics for its “Skin to Believe in” campaign. The world-renowned gymnast hopes to help others overcome the embarrassment and misconceptions that come with visible skin conditions.Through her partnership, the Olympic gold medalist hopes people come forward and speak openly with healthcare providers about their skin troubles, instead of quietly enduring the symptoms or relying on home remedies.“I’ve learned that we can’t fix every problem on our own and it’s okay to seek help,” Biles said in the campaign announcement. This initiative clearly shows how her personal experience inspired Arcutis Biotherapeutics’ awareness campaign.Arcutis and Simone Biles connection explainedArcutis CEO Frank Watanabe said that Biles’ first encounter with Zoryve came organically and started on social media. The decorated gymnast shared her skin problems in a TikTok post during the 2024 Paris Olympics, the CEO said in an interview.Dermatologists recognized her itchy, flaky scalp symptoms as seborrheic dermatitis and encouraged her to explore available treatment options. They encouraged her to check out some of the FDA-approved products available for the condition.That’s how she got started on Zoryve and connected with Arcutis. “She’s a very enthusiastic supporter of the product. Working with her is great,” Watanabe said via Fierce Pharma.Arcutis has worked with other public figures to raise awareness of inflammatory skin conditions - professional golfer Max Homa and actress Tori Spelling, along with her daughter Stella McDermott, in its “Free to Be Me” patient awareness campaign for inflammatory skin conditions.Simone Biles’ stress management tricksHealthline contacted Simone Biles’ dermatologist, Angela Lamb, MD, who said that stress can contribute to eczema flares. Personalized care is essential because weather conditions and individual triggers can also flare symptoms.Beyond treatment, Jonathan Owens’ wife told Healthline that managing stress is a crucial part of health. She spends time with her friends, gets her nails done, enjoys a massage, and takes a bath at night to unwind herself.She also said that stepping away from her demanding gymnastics career helped her relieve her stress. “Honestly, without training every single day, I don’t feel as stressed.” Biles said. “[Everyone] can find different ways to alleviate their stress. And it looks different for everyone.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Carson Beck's Timeline to Become Cardinals QB1 Amid 1-4 Start to Season
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck reportedly may not get a chance to prove himself on the field until later in the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck reportedly may not get a chance to prove himself on the field until later in the 2026 season.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that although he "absolutely" expects Beck to get some playing time this season, sources have indicated that it may not happen until late November, which is when Arizona's schedule gets easier.

Over their next six games, the Cards are at the Los Angeles Rams, home for the Denver Broncos, at the Dallas Cowboys, at the Seattle Seahawks, home for the Rams and at the Kansas City Chiefs.

On Nov. 29, the Cardinals host the Washington Commanders, which could be a softer landing spot for the rookie third-round pick out of Miami.

Arizona also has a three-game stretch against the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders from Weeks 15 through 17, which would give Beck a chance for success.

The Cardinals are currently 1-4, although it wouldn't necessarily be fair to blame veteran starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett for that.

He has done a solid job given the obvious shortcomings of the team as a whole, completing 66.3 percent of his passes for 1,110 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions.

Fellow veteran Gardner Minshew II is actually still listed as Brissett's backup, but Graziano noted that Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made comments Monday that suggest Beck could soon leapfrog him.

Entering the season, it was widely assumed that Beck would get the chance to start a handful of games at some point unless the Cards shocked the football world and got into playoff contention with Brissett at the helm.

Since that appears unlikely, it makes all the sense in the world for Beck to play eventually.

The Cardinals are one of many teams that could be looking to select a quarterback early in the 2027 NFL draft, although the 24-year-old Beck flashing starter potential could possibly change their outlook.

On the flip side, if Beck plays and doesn't look good, Arizona would perhaps be even more convicted in pursuing a new franchise signal-caller.

articles.title: Travis Kelce-backed $200 million Six Flags shares crash 14% to $10.20 after fatal roller coaster accident
articles.summary: Six Flags is facing fresh scrutiny after a fatal roller coaster accident in Georgia sent its shares tumbling to their lowest closing level since 2009.
articles.body: Six Flags is facing fresh scrutiny after a fatal roller coaster accident in Georgia sent its shares tumbling to their lowest closing level since 2009. The death of a father at Six Flags Over Georgia has raised serious questions about ride safety, even as the company prepares to report its next earnings results. The tragedy also comes at a difficult time for the amusement park operator, which has struggled to regain investor confidence. Travis Kelce, who has ties to Six Flags as an ambassador and investor, adds another layer of public interest to the company's latest setback.Six Flags shares fall after fatal Goliath roller coaster accidentSix Flags shares suffered a sharp decline on Tuesday, October 13, after a visitor died on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. The stock closed at $10.20, down around 14% for the day, while reports indicated an intraday decline of more than 16%. It marked the company's lowest closing price since 2009.The victim was identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old father and educator from the Atlanta area. He died on Monday after falling from Goliath, a 200-foot-tall roller coaster known for its high speeds and steep drops.According to local reports, Kariem was riding with his son while his wife and daughter watched from the ground. Witnesses described a horrifying scene as he fell from the ride. Authorities have not yet confirmed what caused the accident.The incident prompted Six Flags to temporarily close nine roller coasters across six parks while safety concerns were assessed. The company also expressed condolences to Kariem's family and said it was cooperating with local authorities investigating the death.“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest’s family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected,” a Six Flags Over Georgia spokesperson told The Post.“The park team and local authorities responded immediately, and we are cooperating fully with local authorities as they complete their investigation. Out of respect for the family’s privacy, we will not be sharing additional details at this time.”Travis Kelce's Six Flags connection comes amid investor concernsThe accident has added pressure to a company already facing financial challenges. Six Flags shares have lost roughly two-thirds of their value over the past three years, according to FactSet. The company's second-quarter earnings report in August also weighed on its stock, and investors are awaiting its next financial update on November 5.Travis Kelce's connection to Six Flags as an ambassador and investor may bring additional attention to the company's fortunes. However, there is no indication that Kelce is involved in the Georgia accident or its investigation.Activist investor Jana Partners has reportedly urged Six Flags to consider a potential sale, highlighting the pressure on management to improve performance.For now, the investigation into Kariem's death remains the central concern. articles.title: Terry Bradshaw hints at retirement, says his time as an NFL analyst is 'coming to an end'
articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw has been a mainstay at Fox for over three decades.
articles.body:
One of the most well-known faces on NFL Sundays knows he's closing in on the end of his career. Long-time NFL analyst Terry Bradshaw hinted at retirement Tuesday, telling "NBC News Daily" he knows his "time on television as a sports broadcaster is coming to an end ."

Bradshaw, 78, appeared on the program discussing his new memoir, which is titled "Looking for Terry." During the interview, Bradshaw was asked about his busy schedule, which is when he said he was nearing the end of his broadcasting journey.

While Bradshaw did not reveal his retirement plans, he will be a significant loss whenever he decides to step away from his current role. After a Hall of Fame playing career — one that saw Bradshaw win four Super Bowls — the quarterback immediately signed a broadcasting deal with CBS in 1984. He was an in-game analyst with the network for years before eventually joining its pregame program in 1990.

Four years later, Bradshaw left the network for the same gig at Fox, where he's remained ever since. Over the years, Bradshaw has established himself as a staple of the network's pregame show "Fox NFL Sunday" where he appears in studio alongside Howie Long, Curt Menefee, Michael Strahan and many others.

While Bradshaw is known for his affable personality, his memoir — which was released Tuesday — focuses on his depression diagnosis, struggles with cancer and failed marriages. The broadcaster said that subject matter made his book a tough sell to publishers, who only wanted to hear stories about football.

For now, Bradshaw is still sharing those stories with fans every Sunday. While his retirement might not be imminent, the long-time analyst knows his on-camera time is approaching its end.

articles.title: President Trump was expected to attend Steelers-Bucs, before his schedule changed
articles.summary: The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game.
articles.body:
The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game. But it ultimately didn't.

On Tuesday, Kristen Holmes of CNN reported that President Trump was expected to attend the Week 6 game between the Steelers and Buccaneers in Tampa. Later in the day, she reported that Trump would not be making the trip .

It would have been the third NFL game attended by Trump during his current term. He was present for Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans between the Chiefs and Eagles. Last year, he attended a Lions-Commanders game in Maryland, making him the first sitting president to attend a regular-season game in nearly 50 years.

Two years ago, in the weeks preceding the election that resulted in his second term, Trump attended a Sunday night game between the Jets and Steelers.

It remains to be seen whether he shows up for an NFL game before the midterm elections, which happen in 20 days. The Commanders are currently scheduled to host the Eagles on Sunday, November 1 — two days before the in-person polls officially open.

articles.title: Bucky Irving amongst most valuable running backs through 5 weeks
articles.summary: Bucky Irving amongst most valuable running backs through 5 weeks
articles.body:
Bucky Irving continues to prove why he is one of the most important players on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Following his dominant performance against the Dallas Cowboys, Irving has established himself as one of the NFL's most impactful running backs, and the advanced analytics back it up. Irving ranks fourth among NFL running backs in rushing Expected Points Added (EPA) through Week 5, sitting at +4.1. Only Kenneth Walker III (+10.9), James Cook (+9.1), and Bijan Robinson (+7.0) rank ahead of him. Irving also finds himself ahead of several established stars, including Christian McCaffrey (+2.7), Jahmyr Gibbs (+1.7), Jonathan Taylor (-0.4), Saquon Barkley (-1.7), and Derrick Henry (-9.3).

EPA measures how much a player's rushing production increases or decreases his team's expected points based on down, distance, and field position. Unlike traditional rushing statistics, it helps show whether a running back is actually improving his offense's chances of scoring rather than simply accumulating yards. Irving's ranking is particularly impressive given Tampa Bay's offensive struggles at the start of the season. The Buccaneers have dealt with inconsistent play calling, difficulty sustaining drives, and a quarterback change following Baker Mayfield's thumb injury. Despite those challenges, Irving has remained one of the few offensive players capable of consistently creating opportunities. His Week 5 performance against Dallas was the perfect example. Irving rushed for a career-high 165 yards on 21 carries, averaging 7.9 yards per attempt while helping Tampa Bay secure its first victory of the season. His ability to turn ordinary rushing attempts into explosive gains completely changed the dynamic of the Buccaneers' offense.

Tampa Bay isn't simply benefiting from giving him the football. His production is helping put the offense in better situations, creating scoring opportunities and taking pressure off rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. For offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, the message should be clear. Irving isn't just another piece of the offense. He is arguably its most important weapon, and his efficiency makes a strong case for continuing to build the rushing attack around him.

articles.title: Packers Could Lose Josh Jacobs for Much Longer Than Expected Due to NFL Rule
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers should perhaps stop expecting Josh Jacobs to return this season and start preparing to play 2026 without him. The post Packers Could Lo...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers don't know when they might get Josh Jacobs back into the lineup, and the NFL rules are murky and unilateral enough that it is not entirely out of the question that the running back misses most, if not all, of the 2026 campaign.

Jacobs faced a couple of misdemeanor charges, one for battery and one for criminal damage to property, following a domestic incident with his former girlfriend in Wisconsin back in May. He pleaded no contest to both charges on September 10, after which the judge handed down punishments that do not include jail time.

The RB's lawyers expedited the hearing in order to wrap the matter up prior to the start of the regular season, which they accomplished. The NFL has typically handed out suspensions in the realm of six games for the type of off-field concerns Jacobs' actions bring with them.

So that was the assumption around the league — that commissioner Roger Goodell would issue a six-to-eight game suspension without pay and Jacobs would return at some point between Weeks 7-9. But with Week 6 just around the corner, the NFL has issued no ruling and Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which is the equivalent of paid leave.

The reason involves video footage of the interaction between Jacobs and his former girlfriend, which the league wants to review before making its determinations. The victim in the case asked the court to seal that evidence permanently, which would have ended the matter. But the judge declined, referring that decision back to the investigating police department that collected the evidence.

There was both an update on that process as well as the revelation of a stipulation in the league's code of conduct policy on Tuesday that indicate Jacobs' absence could stretch on indefinitely.

NFL Still Unable to Review Video Evidence From Josh Jacobs' Legal Case

First, Rob Demovsky of ESPN authored a summary of the police department's decision on the NFL's petition to view the evidence via a public records request.

"An update from the Hobart/Lawrence police department in response to a FOIA request by ESPN for the records in the Josh Jacobs case," Demovsky posted to X Tuesday, October 13 . "To summarize, they determined that 'certain records could be released with appropriate redactions' but that one or more parties (presumably Jacobs and/or the victim) have appealed that decision and therefore nothing will be immediately released."

More or less, that means it could be several more weeks, or even months, before the process is complete and the police release the footage to the NFL — if they ever do. And while this holds off any suspension for Jacobs and allows him to continue on in gainful employment as a member of the Packers organization, it also creates an ongoing obstacle to his return to the field.

NFL May Attempt to Force Josh Jacobs Into Revealing Video Evidence, Even if Legal Process Permanently Seals It

Ken Ingalls, who studies the Green Bay salary cap and reports/posts his work on social media, noted another quirk in the case that fans may sometimes forget, or may not be aware of in the first place.

"Josh Jacobs still sits on the Exempt List, and the video release is still the holdup," Ingalls posted to X on Tuesday . "The league operates on their own standards. Even if the video gets sealed by the legal process, they can still ask/expect Jacobs to willingly share this to them as part of their investigation."

The league can, and has, demanded access to players' and coaches' phone records and other private information in the course of previous investigations involving its code of conduct policy.

It is unclear whether Jacobs still has any copy of the video evidence in question in his possession. If he does, and if the court seals it as evidence not to be shared publicly, which would benefit Jacobs and also appears to be what he wants based on Demovsky's report, it is unclear if the NFL could legally compel the running back to hand over that footage by holding his career hostage.

The unfortunate point for Packers fans is that the sport's worst run game through five weeks ( 60.4 yards per game average and two touchdowns total) does not appear likely to welcome back its RB1 anytime soon.

Let's talk golf integrity & how America needs to do better with putting out – Michael C. has stories to share: I wish it were true that the golf integrity problem just started in the last decade. Unfortunately, it has been going on for a long time. Maybe because today, there are more long-legged blondes on the courses, it's getting more attention. My experience in the pro ams is that many amateurs don't like to admit how high their real handicap is when they play with a pro. I always started off letting the pros know that I was real 18 and that golf was my hobby not my job. The best story I have is one year I was playing in the Sony Pro Am and was paired up with Brett Wetterich and a couple of guys I didn't know. They claimed to be 4 and 6 handicaps. They were obviously lying because they didn't have the mechanics and their shots were all over the course except straight. Halfway through the round, we were about 200 yards from the green with a slight incline. Brett took out a 6 iron and laid it in the middle of the green near the flag. Gee, that fade just went 30 yards offline. For gimmes, no. If everyone is inside of 18", it should not bother pace of play for everyone to putt out. An example why I feel it's important. Was playing a CC course in Fayetteville, NC, during a college tourney. The greens were very fast and rolling. On a dog leg left 5 par, a lake all along the left, I hit a great long iron 2nd to 12". Above the hole. Well, 2nd putt was from 20+ feet. Missed that one too. Oops. Kinda think finishing is important. Well, that's just me. articles.title: NFL does Falcons a favor ahead of Bears matchup
articles.summary: NFL suspends Bears DE Montez Sweat ahead of Week 6 game vs. Falcons
articles.body:
This week the Atlanta Falcons will face a heavyweight NFC contender for the first time this season when they host the Chicago Bears . The bad news is that Chicago has one of the league's best offenses, but the good news is they are vulnerable on defense, and they're going to be missing a big piece this week.

Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended by the league office for two games for violating the NFL's Performance-Enhancing Substances policy, knocking him out for Sunday's matchup at Mercedes-Benz Stadium..

Sweat led the Bears with 10 sacks last season, and they already traded their best interior rusher, Gervon Dexter, to the Falcons just before the season began.

Chicago's current sack leader is second-year defensive end Austin Booker, who has four sacks in five games. Shutting him down would go a long way towards keeping Michael Penix clean and healthy in the pocket, which may be one of the most-important factors in this game.

That said, keeping up with the Bears offense is probably going to be at the top of that list - assuming Caleb Williams returns to the lineup after missing three games with a hamstring injury. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich has to match wits with Ben Johnson, who's one of the best offensive minds in the game.
